An intronic DNA base may be removed during processing, so a mature-junction read need not contain that base. Assigning the product to a particular allele needs suitable linking sequence or another justified allele-specific measurement, with cell-source and reference checks. RNA directly examines the processing product; the gene-level count cannot settle the protein-function question.

before.supportingExcerpt: Among cytosolic ribosomes, some are free and others sit on the cytosolic face of rough ER, outside its lumen. Consider one secreted protein: it enters the ER lumen during synthesis, travels through the lumens of transport vesicles and Golgi compartments, and can leave when a secretory vesicle fuses with the cell membrane. Movement within these membrane-enclosed spaces is not cytosolic escape. This selected route does not describe every protein; a compartment diagram alone does not measure transport, activity or treatment effect.

points.requirement: An early constitutional variant can be inherited or de novo and broadly distributed; a constitutional example is not automatically a gamete/transmission verdict.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Inherited germline variants came through an egg or sperm and are generally present across many tissues. A de novo constitutional variant need not have been inherited from a parent. Changes arising after fertilization can create mosaic distributions. Somatic variants occur in body-cell lineages, including normal tissues as well as cancers. Origin, distribution, harmfulness and transmissibility are separate questions; neither a variant class nor a large read fraction settles them.
evidence.explanation: The inherited versus de novo constitutional distinction is explicit. Origin and broad distribution are kept separate from reproductive-cell involvement and transmission; the illustration is not a hereditary test. Read depth: Complete actual abstracts or individually logged targeted official/review passages and two Dostie PDF pages; no whole primary-paper/protocol or wholesale baseline-claim verification. Construction boundary: Toy examples are hypothetical; colors, geometry, counts and arrows are schematic conventions, not biological frequencies or approval/clinical evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In two invented histories, an early constitutional variant may be inherited or de novo, whereas a later variant can mark a mosaic body-cell lineage, including a normal blood clone. A partial set of sampled cells leaves reproductive-cell involvement and unsampled tumour-cell genotypes unknown. Suppose a cartoon contains two marked blood cells among four and four marked DNA fragments among eight. Those are counts of chosen symbols, not measured allele fractions, a tumour fraction or evidence of inheritance. Plasma fragments are not intact circulating cells, and arrows from blood cells or tumour cells describe possible DNA contributions, not an exhaustive source map or proof of a particular fragment's origin.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Nonsense-mediated decay is RNA surveillance coupled to translation termination. Splicing can leave exon junction protein complexes near later joins in the message. Translation can remove junction-associated proteins; early termination while an appropriate complex remains downstream can help recruit decay machinery in one human route. Stop position, exon architecture, proximity to the start and other transcript features affect susceptibility. A common junction-distance shortcut is a hypothesis, not a universal clinical cutoff.
evidence.explanation: The new already-spliced message separates covalent exon joins from introns and junction-associated protein removal. The hypothetical retained complex is upstream of the later join and downstream of the stop, not at a previously traversed site. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Consider a hypothetical message after splicing: its retained exons are joined in one continuous RNA, without an intron at each join. A translating ribosome has passed an earlier join but stops before a later one. points.requirement: The same fictional gene can yield separate mature A-B-C and A-C processing outcomes across precursor molecules. Retained exons join in order; skipped B does not become an intron, and one RNA is not physically split into both products. Other processing outcomes remain possible.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Imagine separate precursor RNAs from the same fictional gene, with exons A, B and C in that order. One processing outcome retains A-B-C; another joins A directly to C. B is a skipped exon in the second outcome, rather than a region reclassified as an intron. One RNA molecule is not split into both complete products. These are selected outcomes across separate molecules, with other processing possibilities left open. Retained exon sequence can include untranslated regions. The letter pattern alone supplies neither a reading frame nor a guarantee about protein production or RNA decay.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Splicing processes an initial RNA transcript. Exons are retained in a specified product and may contain untranslated sequence; introns are removed. For many nuclear pre-mRNAs, a spliceosome made of RNA and proteins recognizes boundary and regulatory sequences. The donor site starts an intron and the acceptor site ends it. Alternative choices yield transcript isoforms; a variant can alter exon inclusion, intron retention or use of a cryptic site. Exon skipping is not automatically a frameshift: the coding sequence and resulting joins matter. An altered message may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce a changed protein, but neither outcome follows from a prediction alone.

Cancer-associated splicing changes can arise through altered RNA-processing factors or their expression. SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ZRSR2 illustrate studied factors; AR-V7 and BCL2L1 illustrate named transcript contexts. The linked review describes disease-specific mechanisms and therapeutic research. An altered transcript alone does not establish an intact abnormal protein, immune presentation, a therapeutic dependency or patient benefit. Free-drug development and a conjugated payload also require their own construct-specific evidence.

Cell-cycle checkpoints and immune checkpoints describe different biological processes.

points.requirement: Ordered G1-S-G2-M and optional G0/return are distinct from a universal timetable or equal-duration sectors.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: G1 prepares the cell, S copies DNA, and G2 precedes the mitotic phase. Mitosis separates nuclear chromosomes; cytokinesis separates cytoplasm into daughter cells. G0 describes a noncycling state, which need not mean death or loss of function. Cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints regulate transitions, and their alteration can contribute to cancer without making every checkpoint absent or guaranteeing error-free division. Cell-cycle checkpoints and immune checkpoints describe different biological processes.
evidence.explanation: The order, optional G0 and conditional return are explicit. Equal sectors are a layout convention rather than a duration measurement; the field denies that inference. Read depth: Complete actual abstracts or individually logged targeted official/review passages and two Dostie PDF pages; no whole primary-paper/protocol or wholesale baseline-claim verification. Construction boundary: Toy examples are hypothetical; colors, geometry, counts and arrows are schematic conventions, not biological frequencies or approval/clinical evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: On a simplified relative-DNA scale, G1 is the reference amount, S lies between that amount and twice it, and G2 and M before cell separation are about twice it. A G0 branch is optional; return to G1 depends on the cell and conditions. Neither a snapshot nor equally sized sectors establishes phase durations.

The relevant compartments depend on the tissue and disease.

points.requirement: From equal1000 starts to1200 treated and2000 control endpoints, net changes are200 and1000 and the endpoint gap is800. The gap is not800 measured deaths; division and loss remain unmeasured. Nondividing-cell vulnerability is not excluded.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional comparison, two populations start at 1,000 cells and are counted at the same later time. The untreated population reaches 2,000 and the treated one 1,200: their net increases are 1,000 and 200. The 800-cell endpoint difference does not mean that treatment killed 800 cells. Production and loss were not measured separately, so slower division, greater loss or both remain possible explanations. These are arithmetic premises, not a measured drug result or patient-benefit estimate.
evidence.explanation: The exact equal-start counts and endpoint gap are carried. Independent arithmetic confirms the difference is not a measured death count. Gornstein concerns adult mouse sensory-neuron cultures; it supports vulnerability without division within that model, not universal clinical toxicity. Read depth: Complete actual abstracts or individually logged targeted official/review passages and two Dostie PDF pages; no whole primary-paper/protocol or wholesale baseline-claim verification. Construction boundary: Toy examples are hypothetical; colors, geometry, counts and arrows are schematic conventions, not biological frequencies or approval/clinical evidence.

points.requirement: A chemical mark on otherwise identical DNA sequence differs from a base substitution; DNA methylation and histone modifications affect different substrates.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA methylation changes a base’s chemical state without substituting the underlying sequence letter. Much human methylation analysis concerns 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites. Histone modifications affect DNA-associated proteins and are distinct from marks on DNA itself. Some regulatory states persist through division; epigenetic does not mean every mark is permanent or transmitted between generations. Promoter methylation can participate in reduced transcription, while patterns elsewhere need their own interpretation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In an invented sequence example, AACGT can carry a methyl group on its C while the underlying base order remains AACGT. Replacing that C with T instead gives AATGT, a different underlying DNA sequence. Changing a chemical mark on a histone protein is different again. Keep that biological comparison separate from an assay that chemically converts bases: standard bisulfite treatment can change the readout without establishing that the original DNA carried a C-to-T variant. Read the conversion chemistry, locus and cell context before interpreting a methylation call.

points.requirement: A chemical mark on otherwise identical DNA sequence differs from a base substitution; DNA methylation and histone modifications affect different substrates.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: DNA methylation changes a base’s chemical state without substituting the underlying sequence letter. Much human methylation analysis concerns 5-methylcytosine at CpG sites. Histone modifications affect DNA-associated proteins and are distinct from marks on DNA itself. Some regulatory states persist through division; epigenetic does not mean every mark is permanent or transmitted between generations. Promoter methylation can participate in reduced transcription, while patterns elsewhere need their own interpretation.
evidence.explanation: DNA marks and histone modifications affect different substrates; the fictional AACGT/AATGT comparison separates a chemical mark from a sequence substitution. Read depth: Complete actual abstracts or individually logged targeted official/review passages and two Dostie PDF pages; no whole primary-paper/protocol or wholesale baseline-claim verification. Construction boundary: Toy examples are hypothetical; colors, geometry, counts and arrows are schematic conventions, not biological frequencies or approval/clinical evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In an invented sequence example, AACGT can carry a methyl group on its C while the underlying base order remains AACGT. Replacing that C with T instead gives AATGT, a different underlying DNA sequence. Changing a chemical mark on a histone protein is different again. Keep that biological comparison separate from an assay that chemically converts bases: standard bisulfite treatment can change the readout without establishing that the original DNA carried a C-to-T variant. Read the conversion chemistry, locus and cell context before interpreting a methylation call.

points.requirement: An early constitutional variant can be inherited or de novo and broadly distributed; a constitutional example is not automatically a gamete/transmission verdict.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Inherited germline variants came through an egg or sperm and are generally present across many tissues. A de novo constitutional variant need not have been inherited from a parent. Changes arising after fertilization can create mosaic distributions. Somatic variants occur in body-cell lineages, including normal tissues as well as cancers. Origin, distribution, harmfulness and transmissibility are separate questions; neither a variant class nor a large read fraction settles them.
evidence.explanation: The inherited versus de novo constitutional distinction is explicit. Origin and broad distribution are kept separate from reproductive-cell involvement and transmission; the illustration is not a hereditary test. evidence.supportingExcerpt: In two invented histories, an early constitutional variant may be inherited or de novo, whereas a later variant can mark a mosaic body-cell lineage, including a normal blood clone. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Consider a hypothetical message after splicing: its retained exons are joined in one continuous RNA, without an intron at each join. A translating ribosome has passed an earlier join but stops before a later one. An exon junction complex retained upstream of that later join is downstream of the stop and can support the junction-dependent surveillance route. Removing junction-associated proteins during translation is different from removing introns during splicing. In a second hypothetical message the stop lies in the final exon, with no downstream complex specified. That description alone does not measure RNA stability, exclude other decay mechanisms or demonstrate a normal protein. The positions are context for a hypothesis, not a universal distance threshold.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Candidate selection should reconstruct the affected transcript and translated sequence. A stop-gain terminates translation rather than adding a new amino acid; an unchanged upstream sequence alone does not specify a new mutant peptide. Litchfield and colleagues found expressed frameshift changes enriched in positions predicted to escape decay and reported associations with checkpoint outcomes in melanoma cohorts, with additional immune-reactivity evidence from vaccine studies. These are context-specific findings, not a rule that every frameshift is expressed, displayed or useful. Mutant RNA and downstream presentation and recognition remain separate questions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Splicing processes an initial RNA transcript. Exons are retained in a specified product and may contain untranslated sequence; introns are removed. For many nuclear pre-mRNAs, a spliceosome made of RNA and proteins recognizes boundary and regulatory sequences. The donor site starts an intron and the acceptor site ends it. Alternative choices yield transcript isoforms; a variant can alter exon inclusion, intron retention or use of a cryptic site. Exon skipping is not automatically a frameshift: the coding sequence and resulting joins matter. An altered message may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce a changed protein, but neither outcome follows from a prediction alone.

Cancer-associated splicing changes can arise through altered RNA-processing factors or their expression. SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ZRSR2 illustrate studied factors; AR-V7 and BCL2L1 illustrate named transcript contexts. The linked review describes disease-specific mechanisms and therapeutic research. An altered transcript alone does not establish an intact abnormal protein, immune presentation, a therapeutic dependency or patient benefit. Free-drug development and a conjugated payload also require their own construct-specific evidence.
